record.context_brief: one-way multihead automata for string matching
record.original_question: Let Σ be a finite alphabet and let $ be a separator symbol not in Σ. Can a one-way multihead deterministic finite automaton recognize the string-matching language {x$uxv | u, x, v are strings in Σ*}, that is, determine whether an input contains two occurrences of the same pattern x separated as x$uxv? Equivalently, can one-way multihead deterministic finite automata perform string matching?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Can a one-way multihead dfa perform string matching?
More specifically, can such an automaton recognize the language {x$uxvlu, x, v E E*}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\$\notin\Sigma$ be a designated separator symbol. Consider the language
$$L \;=\; \{\, x\,\$\,u\,x\,v \;:\; x,u,v \in \Sigma^{*}\,\} \subseteq (\Sigma\cup\{\$\})^{*},$$
i.e. the set of strings that contain a $\$$ symbol such that some string $x$ appearing immediately before the $\$$ also occurs somewhere after the $\$$.

A one-way multihead deterministic finite automaton with $k$ heads is a finite-state machine equipped with $k$ read-only heads on a single input tape; each head moves only to the right (or stays in place) at each step, the heads cannot write, and the transition function is deterministic, depending on the current state and the tuple of symbols currently scanned by the heads.

Question: Does there exist an integer $k\ge 1$ and a one-way $k$-head deterministic finite automaton that recognizes $L$? Equivalently, can string matching be performed by a one-way multihead deterministic finite automaton?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was settled negatively. Jiang and Li (1996), "k One-Way Heads Cannot Do String-Matching" (J. Comput. System Sci.), proved that for every k, no one-way k-head deterministic finite automaton can recognize the string-matching language, resolving the conjecture posed by Galil and Seiferas. An earlier partial result by Geréb-Graus and Li (1994) handled the case k = 3.

status_evidence.title: k One-Way Heads Cannot Do String-Matching
status_evidence.snippet: A conjecture raised by Galil and Seiferas was settled: k-head one-way deterministic finite automata cannot perform string-matching, for any k nonsensing heads.
status_evidence.claim: Jiang and Li proved that no one-way k-head DFA can perform string matching, settling the question.

status_evidence.title: Three one-way heads cannot do string matching
status_evidence.snippet: Three one-way heads cannot do string-matching, answering the k = 3 case of Galil and Seiferas's question.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier partial resolution for k = 3 by Geréb-Graus and Li.
